name: the rise test goes strict (>), so a rise of exactly 25% no longer warns
expect: a 25% rise (100 -> 125) is a rise

name: the threshold drifts to 50%, so a real 25-33% weekly rise goes unreported — the row's FAILS IF
expect: ⭐ FAILS IF: a 25% rise in the median is reported as RISE in that week

name: the threshold drifts down to 0%, so a 24% rise warns
expect: a 24% rise (100 -> 124) is not a rise

name: the previous week's sample minimum is dropped, so 2 samples read as a measured RISE
expect: 2 samples in the previous week is NOT MEASURED, even over a 9x rise

name: the evaluated week's sample minimum is dropped
expect: 2 samples in the evaluated week is NOT MEASURED

name: the weekly figure becomes the MEAN, so one outlier PR warns
expect: one slow outlier does not move the median into a RISE

name: nothing measured at all reads as rc 0 — a NOT MEASURED week passes as 'no rise'
edits:
if not any(v["status"] == "OK" for v in verdicts):
        return CANNOT_RUN
expect: nothing measured at all is rc 2, never rc 0

name: the zero-baseline guard is dropped, so a 0 s median makes any value a RISE
expect: a 0 s previous median is NOT MEASURED (no percentage exists)

name: the group row takes the LAST shard, not the slowest — wall-clock is under-recorded
expect: ...at a second input: the slowest shard is not the last listed, and a red job counts

name: matrix groups are never derived, so the comparable sweep row disappears
expect: a matrix group gains ONE derived row holding its SLOWEST shard

name: skipped jobs are recorded, dragging medians down for a reason that is not speed
expect: a skipped job and a job with no completed_at are not recorded

name: the append stops being idempotent: a re-run duplicates every row
expect: appending the same rows twice writes them once (re-running never duplicates)

name: the run picker stops filtering by workflow, so the Schema gates run is read as CI
edits: mine = [r for r in runs if r.get("name") == WORKFLOW and r.get("head_sha") == sha]
mine = [r for r in runs if r.get("head_sha") == sha]
expect: pick_ci_run takes the newest CI run on exactly that sha, never another workflow

name: the previous week is two weeks back, so the comparison skips a week
expect: previous_week steps back one calendar week

name: a PR already in the log is fetched again (the skip is dropped)
expect: ...and a PR already in the log is not fetched again

name: the time budget is ignored, so an agent's call runs past the 270 s cap
expect: an exhausted time budget leaves PRs counted as unread, never silently dropped

name: an in-progress run is recorded, freezing a partial PR as done
expect: ...and a run not yet complete is counted, not recorded

name: zero merged PRs reads as a quiet success
expect: 0 merged PRs parsed is rc 2 (nothing parsed), never a quiet success

name: a PARTIAL record exits 0, so the report runs on an incomplete log unannounced
expect: a record cut short by the budget is rc 2 and says PARTIAL

name: --week is ignored and the latest week always evaluated
expect: ⭐ ...and with --week it evaluates THAT week: W40's 24% is no rise, rc 0

name: report_main always exits 0, so a printed WARN never reaches a caller's exit code
expect: ⭐ report_main over a logged rise exits 1 and WARNs for the LATEST week (W45)

name: the default week is the EARLIEST merge, so the tripwire reads an old week
edits: return iso_week(max(r["merged_at"] for r in rows))
return iso_week(min(r["merged_at"] for r in rows))
expect: ⭐ report_main over a logged rise exits 1 and WARNs for the LATEST week (W45)

name: a log line missing a field is accepted, so a corrupt log is read as data
expect: a malformed log line is CANNOT RUN, not skipped

name: the CLI's --report path drops the rule's exit code
edits: return CANNOT_RUN if CANNOT_RUN in (rc_rec, rc_rep) else rc_rep
return CANNOT_RUN if CANNOT_RUN in (rc_rec, rc_rep) else NO_RISE
expect: ⭐ the CLI's --report path reaches the rule: rc 1 and the WARN line

name: the PR query drops --since, so every merged PR ever is fetched and the budget is spent on old weeks
expect: fetch asks gh only for PRs merged on or after --since
